description: Unauthorized API Access Due to Weak Authentication Attackers could attempt to bypass API Gateway authentication by exploiting misconfigured IAM policies, intercepting/stealing API keys, or exploiting authentication vulnerabilities. An attacker obtains an API key through client-side code exposure or intercepts it in transit, then uses it to send unauthorized push notifications to all users.
references: recommendation: Implement robust API authentication and authorization

description: Device Token Exfiltration from DynamoDB Insufficient encryption of device tokens in DynamoDB or overly permissive IAM policies could allow unauthorized access to token data. An attacker exploits an overly permissive IAM role to access DynamoDB and extract device tokens, which are then used to send unauthorized notifications.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1213 - Data from Information Repositories
recommendation: Implement secure token storage and access controls

description: Insecure Direct Lambda Function Access Lambda functions not properly configured within a VPC could be directly invoked if IAM policies are misconfigured. An attacker discovers Lambda function ARNs and exploits misconfigured IAM policies to directly invoke functions, bypassing API Gateway controls.
references: recommendation: Implement proper VPC and network controls

description: Sensitive Data Exposure in CloudWatch Logs Insufficient log sanitization could lead to sensitive data being written to CloudWatch logs, which could then be accessed by unauthorized users with CloudWatch access. An attacker with CloudWatch access discovers sensitive information in logs, including device tokens and notification payloads.
references: mitreATT&CK: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object

description: Insecure Communication Channel with User Devices Without proper encryption and secure communication channels, push notifications could be intercepted or modified in transit. An attacker performs a man-in-the-middle attack to intercept or modify push notifications before they reach user devices.

Token Replay Attacks Device tokens that aren't properly invalidated after use or don't have expiration times could be reused for unauthorized notifications. An attacker captures a valid device token and reuses it multiple times to send unauthorized notifications, even after the token should have been invalidated.
references: recommendation: Implement proper token lifecycle management

description: Analytics Data Pipeline Exposure Misconfigured S3 bucket permissions or Kinesis Firehose delivery settings could expose analytics data to unauthorized users. An attacker discovers an S3 bucket with insufficient access controls and extracts analytics data containing sensitive user information.
